diagnostic:
ACCEPTED. Round 2 of craft for S1 closes the three owed items of whole-candidate review round 1, and both red oracle rows are green at my own run.

THE TWO L8 ROWS. The oracle's own analysis (observation R4 of the delta-2 oracle review) names two independent causes, and both are fixed. One: the folded rail inherited the open rail's scroll box, and a declared overflow-y of auto makes overflow-x compute to auto as well, so the box clipped the revealed word out of view sideways with nothing to scroll it back; [data-nav-collapsed] .sidebar now takes overflow: visible, and the open geometry keeps overflow-y: auto because it draws no flyout and a rail taller than the window must still scroll inside itself (P3 / risk Y5). Two: position: sticky already made .sidebar a stacking context, so the word's z-index: 30 ordered it only inside the rail while .column and .issue-card - positioned, later in the document - painted over it; .sidebar now takes z-index: 20, which is the BAND the design names, above the positioned page content and below the modal at 50, the lane menu at 60, the keyboard-help overlay at 100 and the card drag ghost at 200. The stale comment premise beside the flyout rule (that a positioned descendant with a z-index paints above the non-positioned content column) is rewritten to name the rail's own level instead, and the two bounding rows stay green: the shortcut list is still drawn over the nav, and the open nav still draws no flyout over the board.

LAW L9 AND THE MARK. NavSection::offered_mark(self, is_workspace_admin) -> NavSection is a total, pure, private function on the sum, called ONCE inside resolved() after the rail's own identity read, so the reconciliation is decided in one place and not in the four handlers that name a section. Invites and Tokens become Home exactly when the rail will not offer that member; every other section-by-rights pair keeps the section the page named. This closes failure B1: a render the route gate admitted as a workspace admin whose nav_identity read then failed offers neither admin link and marks Home, so no render carries zero marks. The totality unit test extends over the whole closed product of five sections and the two values of the fact, asserts exactly-one-current for each reconciled mark, and asserts that the reconciled mark is a member the rail offers that identity. Claim strength is what Rust gives here: construction is centralised in the carrier, two marks and zero marks are excluded in the server carrier, and NEITHER is excluded in the template - a predicate applied to the wrong member or a literal aria-current still emits a wrong mark, which is what the shipped mark-carrier check-arch rule and the per-family acceptance rows cover. That open bypass is unchanged by this round.

THE CONTENT-HASH MIGRATION. The stylesheet bytes changed, so foundry.b3a70ff6.css is renamed to foundry.2f9e0cb1.css (first 8 hex of 2f9e0cb13f55fd9d1d1210739a3da9328eba70c9f222039ffbe36ffb7da4233c, recomputed on the final bytes) and the rename travels to all four readers in the same commit: the link in templates/base.html, the row name and sha256 in static/VENDOR.md plus its two prose references, and the three cache-policy assertions in src/lib.rs at 344, 361 and 380. The old name is gone from the tree; cargo xtask check-arch exit 0 confirms every /static reference resolves, every content-hashed filename is its own sha256 prefix and every VENDOR.md sha256 recomputes.

THE CHANGELOG. CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased] gains the entry for this Request in the voice of the shipped entries - a bold operator-facing lead and five sub-items naming the mark on its own page, the two admin links by right, the nav that stays in view on a long page, the short phone bar, and the quiet Sign out and theme control - and it names the re-hashed stylesheet as the shipped v0.19.0 entry does. The stale sentence "Who sees each link has not changed" of the nav-quick-actions entry is corrected to "Who is let into each page has not changed; which of the three the nav offers now follows the operator's rights", which is true: this Request changes what the nav OFFERS and MARKS and changes no route gate.

NO ORACLE, SUPPORT OR DESIGN BYTE CHANGED. git show --stat of the delta touches seven production and document files only. No test was added, weakened, skipped or rewritten except the nav.rs totality test the design declares as a target.

VERIFICATION, all in the Lima VM through scripts/test-in-lima.sh, every step bounded by timeout --kill-after=60, CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=4, stdout and stderr captured to separate files, all lanes in ONE wrapper invocation under its flock and ONE blocking wait with no polling: ui-nav-polish 30 scenarios 30 passed, 194 steps 194 passed, exit 0 (the two previously red word rows included); nav-quick-actions 9/9, 71 steps; nav-collapse-icon-rail 17/17, 106 steps; us-cts-01 8/8, 63 steps; iawr 27/27, 215 steps; cargo xtask check-arch exit 0; cargo test -p foundry-app nav 5 passed 0 failed; cargo xtask smoke printed "xtask smoke :: all gates green". HONEST SEQUENCE: the first run of that script failed cargo fmt --check and therefore smoke (both exit 1) on one over-wrapped matches! expression in the new unit test; the formatter diff was read in the VM, the line was folded by hand, and fmt, the nav unit test and smoke were re-run green. The whole oracle (FOUNDRY_ACCEPTANCE_TAGS=all) was NOT run in this round: not measured. cargo xtask ci was not run; the host owns the recorded verification and nothing was pushed.

REFACTORS: none. No L1-L4 refactor was taken, so no refactor commit precedes the behaviour commit.
